entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2.  By the present Application filed under Section 439(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973,
the Applicant is seeking quashing of the Order dated 4th October 2022 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-2, Nashik in Bail Application No.1145 2022.

Thus in-effect, the Applicant is seeking cancellation of bail granted to the Respondent No.2.
3.

As per the prosecution case, the Applicant was forced to marry Respondent No.2 and for the said purpose, from 2 nd October Dusane 602 APPLN 45.23.DOC 2018 onwards, she was kept in the house of the Accused.

As the Police have refused to register the F.I.R., a private complaint being Criminal Case No. 375 of 2020 was filed and the learned J.MF.C., Sinnar issued process by the Order dated 3 rd April 2021 against the Respondent Nos. 2 to 9 for the offences punishable under Sections 263, 366, 376 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

sentences.text: The Respondent Nos. 2 to 9 filed Application bearing Bail Application No.1145 of 2022 and the learned Additional Sessions Judge by Order dated 17th September 2022 granted interim protection and the same has been confirmed by the Order dated 4 th October 2022 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-2, Nashik.

5. It is the submission of Ms. Kulkarni, learned Counsel for the Applicant that the learned Additional Sessions Judge has recorded the findings which could not have been recorded at the time of passing the Order on Bail Application.
She submits that the same is going to hamper the trial.

In any case,
she submits that the offence is very serious and therefore Anticipatory Bail should not have been granted.
Dusane 602 APPLN 45.23.DOC 6.

Perusal of record shows that the learned Additional Sessions Judge has recorded that prima facie the First Informant i.e. the present Applicant performed love marriage with Respondent No.2 and the case put up by her is prima facie false.

7. Ms. Kulkarni, learned Counsel for the Applicant is right in contending that the learned Additional Sessions Judge should not have at this stage without trial recorded such type of observations and in any case the said observations are only prima facie and same cannot affect the merits of said case and the trial has to be conducted without influenced by said observations.
Even the learend Sessions Judge has also recorded that the observations recorded are prima facie observations.
8. It is required to be noted that the said Order of the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Nashik is dated 4th October 2022.
There is nothing on record to indicate that the protection granted by the learned Additional Sessions Judge is misused.

9. Ms. Kulkarni, learned Counsel states that copy of the Order dated 17th September 2022 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge is not made available to her and she is not aware Dusane 602 APPLN 45.23.DOC which were the terms and conditions, subject to which the interim protection has been granted.
She submits that if this Court is not cancelling the anticipatory bail then appropriate conditions be imposed.

10. Thus, in the facts and circumstances, the Order dated 4 th October 2022 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-2, Nashik in Bail Application No.1145 of 2022 is confirmed subject to the following conditions:-
(i) The Respondent Nos.2 to 9 shall attend the concerned Police Station, as and when called by the Investigating Officer.
(ii) The Respondent Nos.2 to 9 shall furnish their their cell phone numbers and residential address to the Investigating Officer and shall keep the same updated, in case of any change thereto.

sentences.text:
(iii) The Respondent Nos. 2 to 9 shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement,
threat, or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to Dusane 602 APPLN 45.23.DOC dissuade such a person from disclosing the facts to the Court or to any Police personnel.
(iv) The Applicants shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence and shall not contact or influence the Complainant, or any witness, in any manner.
11. The Criminal Application is disposed of accordingly.

12. This Court places on record appreciation of the assistance rendered by Ms. Devyani Kulkarni,
learned Advocate appointed to represent the interest of the Applicant.
The High Court Legal Services Authority is requested to pay her professional charges, as per rules.
